narrative: Material PL1__M69EEF16 exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.56) with 93.5% non-zero working days and a detectable upward trend over the observation window March 2025–March 2026. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.32, mean 4.24 days), requiring a safety stock of 648 units to achieve the 95% service level target. The current SAP policy using the minimum order quantity of 74 units is extremely inefficient, generating ~752 orders per year at a cost of over $75,000 annually; the recommended EOQ of 2,387 units reduces annual total costs by 92% to approximately $5,930 while respecting the storage capacity of 3,876 units.
warnings: Upward demand trend detected — recalibrate mean demand quarterly
Two near-zero lead time observations (0.01, 0.21 days) detected — possible data entry errors
Safety lead time recommendation (2.9 days) is lower than current SAP value (4.0 days) — review before reducing

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Continuous Review — Economic Order Quantity with Stochastic Demand and Lead Time
research_insights.selection_rationale: With 93.5% non-zero demand days and an erratic but largely continuous demand pattern, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is appropriate. EOQ balances the high ordering cost ($100/order) against holding cost, yielding large batch sizes that amortize fixed costs. The standard normal safety stock formula with combined demand and lead-time variance achieves the 95% service level without simulation.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity of 3,875.844 units is satisfied: safety stock (648) + order quantity (2,387) = 3,035 units, leaving 841 units of headroom. No capacity binding. If the upward demand trend continues, the EOQ will grow and the capacity headroom will shrink — monitor annually.
